title: Salt stains on your car carpet: what to do this winter in Calgary
description: Why road salt leaves white rings on car carpet and mats in Calgary, how to keep it from setting in over winter, and when a deep extraction makes sense.
excerpt: Salt and mag chloride ride in on your boots and dry into white rings on the carpet. How to slow it down through the winter and get it out properly.

sections.heading: Where the white rings come from
paragraphs: Once the city starts spreading salt and brine, every trip in and out of the vehicle brings some of it inside. Snow packs into boot treads, melts on the floor, and soaks into the carpet. When it dries, the water leaves and the salt stays behind as a white, crusty ring.

Mag chloride and brine are harder on carpet than plain rock salt. They hold moisture, so the floor stays damp longer, and the residue can feel tacky rather than dry. Left alone, the fibres stiffen and the stain line gets darker each time it gets wet again.

sections.heading: Why it is worth dealing with before spring
paragraphs: A floor that stays damp all winter is where musty smells start. Salt residue also draws in more moisture every time the cabin warms up, so the problem feeds itself through a long Calgary winter of freeze, thaw and freeze again.

The driver's footwell takes the worst of it, but the rear floor and trunk catch plenty too, especially in SUVs and trucks where kids, gear and hockey bags go in and out all week. Getting the salt out mid-season means less to fight in April.

sections.heading: What you can do between details
paragraphs: Rubber or all-weather liners are the single best step. They hold the slush so it doesn't reach the carpet. Empty and rinse them whenever they have standing water, and dry them before they go back in so you aren't trapping melt underneath.

Knock snow off your boots before getting in, and vacuum the dry crust out before it gets wet again. For fresh rings, a damp microfibre with warm water lifts some of the salt. Avoid soaking the carpet, because water that wicks into the padding underneath stays there for a long time when it is cold outside.
Run the heat on the floor setting with the air conditioning on for a few minutes once the cabin is warm. That pulls moisture out of the air and helps the carpet dry instead of fogging the glass.

sections.heading: When it needs a proper extraction
paragraphs: Once rings have built up in layers, wiping only moves the salt around. Extraction dissolves the residue, flushes it out of the fibres and pulls the dirty water back out of the carpet and mats, so the salt actually leaves the vehicle instead of drying back in.

sections.heading: Timing it through the season
paragraphs: Most drivers do well with one deep clean partway through winter and another once the streets are swept in spring. If the vehicle is a daily commuter or a family hauler, a regular visit keeps the salt from ever setting in. The Xpress Pass puts that on a schedule so you don't have to remember to book it.

faqs.q: Will salt stains come out of car carpet completely?
faqs.a: Fresh and moderate salt rings usually extract cleanly. Rings that have built up over several winters can leave some discoloration in light carpet, which we will point out before starting.

faqs.q: Can you clean the interior in winter if it's cold out?
faqs.a: Yes. The vans carry their own water and power, and a garage or covered spot helps in the coldest weeks. We will let you know about drying time so the carpet is not left damp in the cold.

faqs.q: Do rubber floor liners stop salt stains?
faqs.a: They catch most of it, but salt still gets onto the carpet around the edges, on the seat sides and in the rear footwells. Liners make the deep clean easier, not unnecessary.
